title: A Cipher for the Alibi
premise: Retired detective Astrid Okafor has built a quiet life around his failing bookshop and the unofficial cases he solves from behind the counter, but a confession letter postmarked the day after a funeral shatters his anonymity: it names him, praises his methods, and promises a fourth death timed to the opening of a murder trial. The letter's author is someone with intimate access to the police case file, forcing Astrid to work alongside the young prosecutor he once mentored while hiding his own history of vigilante justice. As Astrid lays a trap using the cipher hidden in the letter, he discovers the killer is the trial's own court clerk, corrupting evidence for a powerful family, and that the intended fourth victim is the star witness. In the climax, Astrid sacrifices his invisibility, testifying to his past to expose the tampering, and ends the book choosing his found family of misfit regulars over the shadow life he treasured.
about_author: O. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former small-town court reporter who spent fifteen years watching justice bend in real time before turning to fiction. They live above a secondhand bookshop and insist, unprompted, that every plot twist in their novels has happened at least once in an actual courtroom.

chapters.title: The Postmark Problem
chapters.summary: Astrid Okafor, POV. Three weeks after closing the unofficial case of drowned fisherman Elias Vann, Astrid receives a letter confessing to the death—postmarked the day after the funeral. The letter quotes details never made public and addresses him by his old detective nickname. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in flattery; the past has found his address.

chapters.title: Regulars and Ruin
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with interludes from shop assistant Nia. We meet the found family: Nia, ex-con baker Theo, and insomniac widow Mrs. Pell, who keep the failing bookshop alive. Astrid secretly verifies the letter against his private notes and realizes the writer knows the official file better than he does. Beat: warmth sharpening into fear as he understands someone inside the system is watching.

chapters.title: What the File Forgot
chapters.summary: Astrid visits prosecutor Dani Reyes, his former protégé, under the guise of donating old casebooks. He probes the upcoming Harrow trial—the drowning's official framing—and notices the evidence log has gaps matching the letter's knowledge. Beat: the ache of mentoring someone who must never learn how he really solved those three deaths.

chapters.title: A Cipher in Plain Ink
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. While shelving returns, Nia spots that the letter's odd capitalizations map to page-and-line numbers in a specific edition stocked in the shop—a book Astrid sold exactly one copy of. Beat: the thrill of the hunt infecting the whole shop family, and Astrid's guilt at endangering them.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Decoded, the cipher predicts a fourth death: 'the one who speaks.' Astrid realizes the target is Marisol Quist, the Harrow trial's star witness. He tries to warn her through channels that won't reveal him, but she trusts no one—least of all police. Beat: isolation; justice outside the law means no protection detail, no badge, no backup.

chapters.title: Trial by Water
chapters.summary: Dani Reyes's POV. The Harrow trial opens, and evidence goes subtly wrong: a lab report re-dated, a chain-of-custody form initialed by someone who wasn't there. Dani suspects clerical sabotage but can't prove it, and her requests for help are stonewalled upstairs. Beat: institutional power flexing; Dani's faith in the system cracking.

chapters.title: Mrs. Pell Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Mrs. Pell's POV. The sharp-eyed widow recognizes the court clerk, Gerald Finch, as a man who once tried to buy a first edition from the shop—and who lingered over Astrid's locked back room. She reports it to Astrid, who realizes Finch accessed his private files during a 'building inspection.' Beat: rage and violation; the watcher was watched.

chapters.title: Bait from a Dead Man's Shelf
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid plants a false cipher in a decoy letter, letting it be 'discovered' through Finch's channels, promising the witness will be moved alone on Thursday night. He tells Nia, Theo, and Mrs. Pell the truth about his past cases—betting his found family on honesty. Beat: vulnerability repaid with loyalty; the shop becomes a war room.

chapters.title: Thursday Night
chapters.summary: Alternating Astrid and Dani POVs. The trap springs: Finch comes for Marisol, armed with the corrupted file that was supposed to discredit her testimony, and finds Astrid instead—with Dani arriving to arrest him properly. Finch reveals the powerful Harrow family paid him, believing themselves untouchable. Beat: climax; violence narrowly averted, truth dragged into the light.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the reopened hearing, Astrid takes the stand, exposing the tampered evidence and confessing his own extralegal investigations, trading his anonymity for Marisol's safety and Finch's conviction. The Harrow family's influence begins to unravel. Back at the bookshop, the regulars repaint the sign together. Beat: resolution; justice outside the law finally walks through the front door, and Astrid lets it.
